summary: A number you track over time to see whether an aim is being met.
example: Quality pass rate: 62 percent today, aiming for 75 percent by June 2027.
definition: A KPI (key performance indicator) is a number you track over time to see whether an aim is being met. It says what is counted, in what unit, which way is better, where the number comes from and how often it is read. Its baseline is today's figure and its target is the figure to reach, each with a date. The figure for each period is kept separately, as a reading. A KPI is not a key result (a number written on one aim), not an aim, not a single reading, and not a data source (where the number comes from).

cues.kpi: the name of a number to measure, such as a rate, a share, an average or a count

/spec/metric/measure/counts.guide: What is counted or added up, in your own words: the thing, not a column. An analyst maps it to the data later.

/spec/metric/where.guide: Only the rows that count, each as what is compared, how, and the value, such as the depot's region is north. Leave it empty to count every row.

/spec/definition.guide: Exactly what is counted, where and when. Leave out the target.
good: Share of deliveries meeting the quality standard at intake.
Median hours between a delivery being taken in and being collected from the depot.
Share of intake weight lost between the depot and the buyer in a season.

poor.why: Not countable as written: good by what standard, checked where?
Pass what, checked where? A check at intake and a check at the buyer give different numbers.

poor.text: Share of deliveries meeting the standard at intake, which should reach 75 percent.
poor.why: The target belongs in the target field; the definition says only what is counted.

/spec/unit.guide: The unit the number is counted in, such as percent, count, hours or days. Add a new unit only if none fits.

poor.why: What is counted belongs in the definition; the unit is count.

/spec/direction.guide: Whether the number should go up, go down or stay the same.

/spec/goals.guide: The aims this number shows progress on, most often outcomes. Link only aims this number shows are met.

poor.why: Earnings move for many reasons, so the number cannot say whether faults are now found before dispatch.

poor.text: Every goal the measure might touch
poor.why: Link only the aims this number shows are met, not every related one.

/spec/resultLevel.guide: What this number shows: an output (something the work produced), an outcome (something that changed because of it), or an impact (the longer-term change).

poor.why: Turnaround is what the collection service produces, an output. Less harvest lost is the longer-term change.

/spec/baseline/value.guide: Today's figure. If it has not been measured yet, say why and when it will be, instead of guessing.

poor.why: Zero is a real figure. If it has not been measured, mark it unknown and say why.

/spec/baseline/date.guide: The month the baseline was measured, before the target's month.

/spec/target/value.guide: The figure you want to reach.
good: 20 hours, for Collection turnaround, whose direction is decrease

poor.why: Above the baseline of 41 on a measure whose direction is decrease: the target moves the wrong way.

/spec/target/date.guide: The month you want to reach the target by.

/spec/cycle.guide: How often the number is read, such as monthly or each season. Pick one your data source can keep up with.
good: seasonal-cycle, for Quality pass rate, read from forms transcribed each season
monthly-cycle, for Collection turnaround, read from a log kept weekly

poor.why: Its source is transcribed once a season, so most monthly periods would have nothing to read.

/spec/disaggregations.guide: What the number is split by, such as depot, region or product line. Leave it empty if you report only the total.
good: region and product-line, for Quality pass rate

poor.why: A group of people the work is for, not a way to split the number.
Time is already covered by how often the number is read.

/metadata/name.guide: The name people use for this number.

/spec/baseline/unknownReason.guide: Why today's figure is not known yet.
good: The loss survey has never been run at the northern depots; the first one closes in March.

poor.why: Does not say why the figure is missing or when it will be known.

/spec/baseline/expectedBy.guide: The month you expect to know the figure.

/spec/sources.guide: Where the number comes from. Add more than one if it is worked out from several.

poor.why: Members' opinion of quality is a different number from the share of deliveries meeting the standard at intake.

/spec/owner.guide: The role or team responsible for this number: it collects the readings and explains them. Name a role, not a person.
good: {"kind":"Resource","id":"quality-team-unit"}, a unit answering as a whole

Gap:/spec/measure.ask: Which gap does this KPI track?
Gap:/spec/measure.ifNone: Leave it empty if this KPI does not track a known gap. If it tracks one not yet recorded, add that gap and pick this KPI for it.

KPIReadings:/spec/kpi.ask: Where are this KPI's readings kept? Each KPI has one list of readings, one per period.
KPIReadings:/spec/kpi.ifNone: Choose how often the KPI is read first, then add a reading for the first period that has ended.

checks.kpi-baseline: Record today's figure and the date it was measured. If nobody knows it yet, say why and when it will be known.
checks.kpi-target: Set the figure to reach and the date to reach it by.
checks.kpi-cycle: Choose how often it is read.
checks.kpi-aligned: Name the aims this number shows progress on.
